# Walter Blythe

## Overview

- **Status:** alive  _(assumed)_
- **Family:** [Jem](../character/jem.md) (sibling)

## Appearance

Considered the handsomest of the [Ingleside](../codex/places.md#ingleside) children, he features straight black hair and finely modelled facial features. He is further distinguished by his great, splendid, and dark gray eyes.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER III. THE INGLESIDE CHILDREN P12](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0012), [v5 CHAPTER III. THE INGLESIDE CHILDREN P13](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0013), [v5 CHAPTER VIII. MISS CORNELIA INTERVENES P25](../source/v05-c08.md#nw-v05-c08-p0025)_

## Personality

Driven by a vivid imagination and a passionate love of beauty, Walter possesses a day-dreaming nature and a deep affection for ghost stories. He harbors a ambition to become a poet himself and already writes poetry, alongside demonstrating an ability to pray remarkably well and talk "book talk." Though he harbors a dramatic instinct to thrill others with his words, he possesses a tender disposition, taking blame upon himself and holding a strong aversion to ugly conflict, fighting, and physical pain. He hates being hurt himself and cannot bear to see other things get hurt. He also harbors longings to see the Nile and the Sphinx, and is motivated to protect his mother and [Faith Meredith](../character/faith.md) from insults.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER III. THE INGLESIDE CHILDREN P13](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0013), [v5 CHAPTER III. THE INGLESIDE CHILDREN P14](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0014), [v5 CHAPTER IV. ## History

Walter Blythe developed an early love for poetry, spending his childhood reading poets after learning to read and winning a school poem-writing prize. He spent much of his time gathering with his siblings and the Meredith children in [Rainbow Valley](../codex/places.md#rainbow-valley), where he read mythic stories aloud and discussed the [Pied Piper](../character/pied-piper.md). When [Dan Reese](../character/dan-reese.md) hurled insults at [Faith Meredith](../character/faith.md) and Walter's mother, Walter reluctantly agreed to a fight, overcoming his intense dread to defeat Dan after school. Following the fight, Walter received approval from Mr. Meredith and comforting support from his mother.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER III. THE INGLESIDE CHILDREN P4](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0004), [v5 CHAPTER III. THE INGLESIDE CHILDREN P7](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0007), [v5 CHAPTER III. ## Quotes

> "But I’m not going to be frightened any more, sir. Being frightened of things is worse than the things themselves. I’m going to ask father to take me over to Lowbridge to-morrow to get my tooth out."
>
> — Walter Blythe — [v5 CHAPTER XVII. A DOUBLE VICTORY P71](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0071)

> “I never fought before—and I didn’t want to right up to the last—and then,” said Walter, determined to make a clean breast of it, “I liked it while I was at it.”
>
> — Walter Blythe — [v5 CHAPTER XVII. A DOUBLE VICTORY P68](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0068)

> "It would be a big pain. I hate being hurt. Father said he wouldn’t insist on my going—he’d wait until I’d made up my own mind to go."
>
> — Walter Blythe — [v5 CHAPTER XVI. TIT FOR TAT P14](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0014)

> "I didn’t say I would run. I said I wanted to run. That’s a different thing. I want to help people, too. But oh, I wish there weren’t any ugly, dreadful things in the world. I wish everything was glad and beautiful."
>
> — Walter Blythe — [v5 CHAPTER XVI. TIT FOR TAT P18](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0018)

> "The flower angel’s aren’t. They are a pale misty blue, just like the haze in the valley. Oh, how I wish I could fly. It must be glorious."
>
> — Walter Blythe — [v5 CHAPTER III. THE INGLESIDE CHILDREN P22](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0022)

## Relationships

### [Dan Reese](../character/dan-reese.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/dan-reese--walter-blythe.md)

[Dan Reese](../character/dan-reese.md) is a schoolboy opponent of Walter Blythe. The hostility between them peaked when Dan hurled insults at [Faith](../character/faith.md) and Walter's mother, [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md). Walter confronted Dan and agreed to a fistfight after school the following evening, which Walter won despite his internal dread.

### [John Meredith](../character/john-meredith.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/john-meredith--walter-blythe.md)

[John Meredith](../character/john-meredith.md) is a minister and close friend to Walter Blythe with whom he talks unreservedly. After Walter's fight with [Dan Reese](../character/dan-reese.md), Mr. Meredith met him in [Rainbow Valley](../codex/places.md#rainbow-valley) and expressed his approval of Walter standing up and fighting for a good cause.
